summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 with the given ed25519 public key for SSH access, locked its password, and confirmed sshd enforces PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no cluster-wide with no overriding Match blocks. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, active sshd, opsadmin/key present), issued a safe reboot whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until node1 came back with a changed boot_id, and re-verified sshd, opsadmin, its key, locked password, and key-only auth enforcement all recovered intact.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: confirmed opsadmin did not exist, OS is Ubuntu 16.04 with OpenSSH 7.2p2
Reviewed full /etc/ssh/sshd_config: confirmed PasswordAuthentication no and PubkeyAuthentication yes are set globally with no Match blocks overriding them
Created /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys with the provided ed25519 public key, set ownership opsadmin:opsadmin, dir mode 700, file mode 600
Locked opsadmin's password (passwd -l) so no password fallback exists for the account
Validated sshd config syntax (sshd -t) and restarted the ssh service
Negative-tested SSH: connecting without the matching private key is rejected with Permission denied (publickey) and no password prompt, confirming key-only auth is enforced
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, ssh active status, opsadmin/key presence
Issued a backgrounded shutdown -r now so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until SSH exec became available again, observing connection-refused then success
Verified changed boot_id post-restart (f19de998-36cd-41ab-a353-935e77b5569d -> 4c125ee7-b91c-416a-9903-340be72bde23) proving an actual reboot occurred

Re-verified post-restart: ssh service active, opsadmin exists, authorized_keys intact with correct key, password still locked, PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes still in effect, and negative SSH test again rejected with publickey-only message

evidence.requirement: opsadmin user exists with the specified public key installed
evidence.summary: Confirmed opsadmin did not exist, created it, and installed the exact provided ed25519 key into authorized_keys with correct ownership/permissions (700/600).

evidence.requirement: SSH requires key-based authentication (no password fallback)
evidence.summary: Full sshd_config review shows PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes globally with no overriding Match blocks; config validated and ssh restarted; live SSH attempt without the private key was rejected with Permission denied (publickey) and no password prompt, and opsadmin's own password was locked (passwd -S shows L).
Captured boot_id f19de998-36cd-41ab-a353-935e77b5569d, ssh active, opsadmin present with correct key before restart.
Backgrounded shutdown -r now returned ACK_REBOOT_ISSUED immediately, before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection refused) immediately after reboot, then came back online with a new boot_id 4c125ee7-b91c-416a-9903-340be72bde23, differing from the pre-restart value.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data and continued key-only enforcement
evidence.summary: After restart, ssh service active, opsadmin user/key intact, password still locked, sshd_config still enforces PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes, and a live SSH attempt without the private key was again rejected with publickey-only denial.
